rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The false-blood shirt marks the beginning of Jacob’s grief, while Joseph’s later shirt marks its end.
rows.anchor: الأمر الآخر أنه استُعمل بداية لحزن يعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph’s shirt is evidence at three stages: his separation into slavery, imprisonment after the Aziz’s wife incident, and reunion with his family.
rows.anchor: استعمل القميص بيّنة في ثلاث مواضع واستعمل لثلاث مراحل زمنية معاشية في حياة يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob identifies Joseph by the shirt’s scent; the author argues that people have distinctive odors that can serve as evidence even over long distances.
rows.anchor: لكل إنسان له رائحة خاصة لكن لا يميزها كل الناس وإنما تميزها الكلاب البوليسية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting هم restricts the negation to the believers: they do not grieve, while people of misguidance remain in grief; the alternative ما ضربته would deny the act by anyone.
rows.anchor: بتقديم (هم) الذين يحزن غيرهم وليس هم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two clauses negate both established fear and emerging grief; he says this combination conveys the intended sense better than alternative wording.
rows.anchor: نفي الخوف المتجدد والثابت ونفى الحزن المتجدد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Commerce comes first because the arriving caravan drew people from the Friday sermon during high prices; diversion comes first later because it distracts people more generally.
rows.anchor: قدّم التجارة في أول الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting هم particularizes the negation of grief to the addressed believers and implies that others grieve.
rows.anchor: بتقديم (هم) الذين يحزن غيرهم وليس هم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects لا عليهم خوف because it would imply that fear lies upon others, raising the question of who could fear for the unbelievers.
rows.anchor: لذا لا يصح أن يقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative لا خوفَ explicitly negates the whole class; nominative لا خوفٌ can mean either the whole class or a single fear, with praise context selecting comprehensive negation.
rows.anchor: لا النافية للجنس تفيد التنصيص في نفي الجنس

rows.speaker: يعقوب
rows.claim: Yaʿqūb has a reading with the accusative خوفَ instead of the nominative خوفٌ.
rows.anchor: قراءة أخرى (خوفَ) - قراءة يعقوب

words: إِن كَانَ قَمِيصُهُ قُدَّ مِن قُبُلٍ
rows.speaker: النحاة
rows.claim: Grammarians say conditional clauses refer to the future, even when the verb appears in the past tense; the author says this is generally, but not invariably, true.
rows.anchor: جواب الشرط عند النحاة أن الشرط استقبال

words: إِن كَانَ قَمِيصُهُ قُدَّ مِن قُبُلٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects the future-only rule as absolute: the shirt condition and إن افتريته فعلي إجرامي concern a past or unrealized past, and he also gives a conditional example about keeping a prior promise.
rows.anchor: وأنا أرى أنه في الغالب هذا صحيح ولكنه ليس قاعدة عامة

words: إِن كَانَ قَمِيصُهُ قُدَّ مِن قُبُلٍ
rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: A poet lamenting his sons supplies a counterexample: the conditional إن يهلك بني refers to their possible death, not a future condition imposed by the rule as the author frames it.
rows.anchor: قول الشاعر وهو يرثي أبناءه، هو على قبرهم يرثيهم يقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Allah is used in contexts of severe warning, obligation, and threat; Rabb highlights lordship, nurture, guidance, and blessings bestowed on all people, so guidance often appears with Rabb.
rows.anchor: لفظ الجلالة الله هو اللفظ العام لله تعالى ويذكر هذا اللفظ دائماً في مقام التخويف الشديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He tentatively suggests the Prophet received divine vision, perhaps with ordinary vision suspended or with sight stronger than human capacity, citing his seeing the caravan, Moses in his grave, and Gabriel.
rows.anchor: قد يحتمل المعنى أن الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He parses al-shuḥḥ as the second object of a verb that takes two objects, with the souls as passive subject (or first object), meaning avarice was brought to the souls.
rows.anchor: فعل أحضر يأخذ مفعولين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He pictures God as creating the souls with avarice and placing it within them.
rows.anchor: وكأن الله تعالى أحضر الأنفس عندما خلقها خلق الشح وجعله فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final mark in ليكوناً is the light emphatic nūn, not tanwīn; at pause it is written with an alif and may be represented by tanwīn.
rows.anchor: هذه ليست تنوين وإنما هي نون التوكيد الخفيفة إذا وقف عليها يوقف عليها بالألف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavy emphatic nūn in imprisonment makes that outcome more certain than Joseph’s becoming one of the humiliated.
rows.anchor: نون التوكيد الثقيلة وهي مؤكدة أكثر من الخفيفة وقد دلّت في المعنى أن دخوله السجن آكد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse has two authentic mutawātir readings, with geminated ربّما and ungeminated ربما; both are valid Arabic forms.
rows.anchor: إحداهما مشددة (ربّما) والأخرى مخففة (ربما)

rows.speaker: قسم
rows.claim: One group says رُبّ indicates abundance or frequency.
rows.anchor: قسم قالوا أنها تفيد التكثير

rows.speaker: قسم
rows.claim: Another group says رُبّ indicates scarcity or rarity, which the author describes as its general sense, adjusted by context.
rows.anchor: وقسم قال إنها تفيد التقليل وهذا معناها على العموم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ungeminated form is less forceful in either frequency or rarity than the geminated form, so ربّما conveys a stronger degree than ربما.
rows.anchor: (رب) في معناها أقل في التقليل والتكثير من (رُبّ)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wish could arise in worldly life when unbelievers see spoils such as Badr’s, or in the afterlife when they see believers’ reward; the two readings span weak and intense wishing across both settings.
rows.anchor: وكلمة (ربما) تحتمل أن تكون قد قيلت في الدنيا عندما رأوا الغنائم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wa joins items without ordering them; fa indicates ordered immediate succession, while thumma marks ordered succession after a delay.
rows.anchor: أما استخدام الواو كما في قولنا جاء محمد وخالد لا تفيد الترتيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Death is reinforced by both inna and lām, while resurrection has inna alone; grammarians say imperfect-tense lām makes the verb present-oriented and therefore unsuitable for future resurrection, though he questions their account elsewhere.
rows.anchor: جاء التوكيد في الآية 15 مع ذكر الموت بـ (إنّ) واللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Joseph’s threat, the nūn is emphatic and assigns the verbs to the future; the lām is the oath lām, not a lām of emphasis.
rows.anchor: النون نون التوكيد التي تخلص الفعل للمستقبل واللام هي لام القسم وليست لام التوكيد هنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tāʾ is an oath particle restricted to the name Allah; it occurs five times in the Qur’an, three in Joseph and twice in al-Naḥl.
rows.anchor: التاء حرف قسم مثل الواو لكن التاء تكون مختصّة بلفظ الجلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tāʾ in this oath conveys veneration and is etymologically a substitution for wāw, which is commonly used to swear by other things such as dawn, forenoon, night, and sun.
rows.anchor: والتاء في أصلها اللغوي مُبدلةٌ من الواو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥukm can mean wisdom or judgment; knowledge alone does not necessarily make someone wise or a judge, but God granted Joseph wisdom, knowledge, and judicial authority together.
rows.anchor: الحكم يأتي بمعنى الحكمة وبمعنى القضاء وليس بالضرورة لمن أوتي العلم أن يكون حكيماً أو قاضياً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph’s brothers did not ask him to forgive them or name their offense, using a light إن; to their father they explicitly requested forgiveness and admitted their sins emphatically with إنّا.
rows.anchor: هم لم يسألوه المغفرة وإنما هو الذي دعا لهم بالمغفرة دون أن يسألوه حتى أنهم لم يذكروا الخطيئة التي ارتكبوها بحق يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob promises delayed intercession because his sons’ deed caused him greater lasting suffering, including blindness and grief; unlike Joseph, he had not ceased to feel its pain.
rows.anchor: أما تأثير فعلة إخوة يوسف على أبيهم فكان أعظم لأنه أصيب بالعمى والأسى والحسرة على ولده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph immediately absolves his brothers and asks God to forgive them because their act ultimately benefited him.
rows.anchor: لأنه استفاد من فعلة إخوته معه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣuwāʿ is treated as masculine in one passage and feminine in another; Arabic allows some nouns to be either gender, with grammatical feminine being metaphorical.
rows.anchor: فاستخدمت كلمة (صواع) مرة مذكرة ومرة مؤنثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He illustrates flexible grammatical gender with al-ʿāqiba, masculine when used for punishment and feminine when used for a cry.
rows.anchor: فكلمة (العاقبة) مثلاً تُذكّر إذا استعملت للعذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the context of a charitable loan, karīm means a reward of excellent and complete goodness.
rows.anchor: الأجر الكريم هو الأجر الحسن البالغ الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier verse asks for both faith and spending and thus calls the reward great; the broader set of demands corresponds to the larger reward.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية طلبين هما: آمنوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fatir repeats the preposition before al-zubur and al-kitāb for emphasis and detail in a sustained warning and preaching context; Ali ʿImran omits it for concision while answering a specific historical claim.
rows.anchor: المقام في سورة فاطر مقام التوكيد والتفصيل بخلاف ما ورد في سورة آل عمران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khidr attributes the boat’s defect to himself because God is not associated with a flaw; Abraham similarly says that when he becomes ill, God heals him rather than saying God made him ill.
rows.anchor: جاء استعمال فعل (أردت) مع خرق السفينة لأن الله تعالى لا ينسب العيب إلى نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The boy’s episode combines evil, killing an innocent person, with good, replacement by a better child, so the action is attributed with the plural أردنا.
rows.anchor: أما في حادثة الغلام ففيها جانب شر وهو قتل نفس زكية بغير نفس وجانب خير وهو الإبدال بخير منه فأصبح فيها مشترك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wall episode is wholly good—the treasure is preserved for two orphans of a righteous father—so the action is attributed directly to God.
rows.anchor: فالأمر كله خير فتحت الجدار كنز وأبو الغلامين كان صالحاً والأمر كله خير ليس فيه جانب سوء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects calling shirʿa a verbal noun or minhāj an instrument noun: shirʿa is a route to water, and minhāj is a clear, straight path.
rows.anchor: ليس في الآية اسم مصدر ولا اسم آلة لأن الشرعة ليست اسم مصدر والمنهاج ليست اسم آلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabs call the water source sharīʿa; as water gives transient life, religion gives eternal life, and both serve to refresh and purify.
rows.anchor: العرب تسمي شريعة مورد الماء الذي لا ينقطع وسبب التسمية لأن الماء به سبب الحياة الفانية والدين سبب الحياة الأبدية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pattern mifʿāl can name an instrument, source, time, or place; minhāj is not an instrument but a clear, straight path, distinct from sabīl, leading to eternal life.
rows.anchor: صيغة مفعال فلا تختص بالآلة فقد تكون آلة (مهباج) وقد تكون مصدراً

rows.speaker: قالوا
rows.claim: They explain benefit preceding harm in 13:16 by its preceding order طوعاً وكرهاً in 13:15; in Sabaʾ, benefit precedes harm after mention of God’s expanding provision.
rows.anchor: فقدّم النفع على الضرر، قالوا: وذلك لتقدم قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur’anic passages often mention mercy before punishment, including forgiveness before punishment, and this ordering is echoed in a report that divine mercy preceded wrath.
rows.anchor: حيث ذكر الرحمة والعذاب بدأ بذكر الرحمة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet quotes God as saying, My mercy preceded My wrath.
rows.anchor: قول النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - حكاية عن الله تعالى
